title: `lite upgrade --target local` from a file-backed Supalite source does not carry the serial-sequence position, so the first post-upgrade insert collides
rationale: Reproduced this sprint against real targets in packages/targets/test/integration/upgrade-local.test.ts. `@supabase/lite@0.9.0`'s local-upgrade data phase (Li()/mx() in dist/cli/index.js) only emits `SELECT setval(pg_get_serial_sequence(...))` for a column whose live introspection shows a `nextval(` default or a literal serial/bigserial type. When the upgrade SOURCE is a file-backed Supalite target (supalite-sqlite-postgres, driver=sqlite-postgres), the underlying SQLite introspection exposes neither — the deparse cache records the bigserial column as `isSerial:false, defaultValue:null` — so lite migrates the row ids (id 1..N) but leaves the destination sequence at its start value. The first post-upgrade `INSERT ... (label) VALUES (...)` on the Supabase-local destination then draws `nextval` = 1 and fails with `duplicate key value violates unique constraint`. A plain Supalite clone of the same source (baseline B) is unaffected: its next insert lands at N+1. UPGRADE.md's 'Sequence resets after all migrated user data has been inserted' holds for pglite/postgres sources but not for the file-backed sqlite/sqlite-postgres sources. `supadiff verify-upgrade` records this as check `sequence-next-use` = `divergence` (not a failure) and realigning the sequence is left to the operator (`SELECT setval(pg_get_serial_sequence('public.<table>','id'), (SELECT max(id) FROM public.<table>))`).

evidence.value: sequence-next-use check detail: B (Supalite clone) next insert advances past the migrated ids; C (after real `lite upgrade`) next insert fails with duplicate key / does not advance. Reproduced in packages/targets/test/integration/upgrade-local.test.ts.

Deparse cache for a bigserial column on driver=sqlite-postgres: {"isSerial":false,"defaultValue":null,"pgTypeName":"int8"} — lite's mx() sequence-reset predicate sees no serial default. docs/DIVERGENCES.md, docs/LIMITATIONS.md.
